W.note: Syllables are 5-7-5 exactly (Midwin-ter ridge wind / one lens o-ver the pale peak / holds while air runs through), and a lenticular cloud held over a peak while wind passes through it is accurately evoked; line 1 reads as a slightly clipped fragment.

X.note: Syllables are 5-7-5 exactly (pearl-lit high un-seen / na-cre-ous clouds bloom at dusk / win-ter's rar-est sky), and nacreous clouds are a true rare high-altitude winter dusk phenomenon, but 'rarest sky' and 'bloom' are stock phrasing and the close is a flat declaration.

Y.note: Syllables are 5-7-5 exactly (na-cre-ous glow spreads / a-cross the win-ter dusk sky / clouds no one ex-pects); nacreous is accurate, but 'glow spreads across the sky' is generic and 'clouds no one expects' is a glib tag line with little feeling behind it.

Z.note: Syllables run 5-7-6 (win-ter ridge one lens / holds still in the mov-ing wind / its cold edge sharp on blue), so the last line is one syllable long, but the lenticular image and the still-in-moving-wind turn are vivid and true.
